passage:
Note on Mohit, written by Gurpreet, class mentor.

Mohit has missed class on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday. On Wednesday I found out from his roommate that he had deleted all his accounts after a wave of hostile comments and had not left the room since. He said he wanted to disappear from everything.

I went to the hostel that afternoon and sat on the floor by his bed. I told him this was not his fault and that I was glad he'd opened the door. I explained that deleting everything also removes the record that would help, and that we could still ask the platform and the college for help. With his agreement, I walked him to the counsellor that same day and stayed while they spoke.

qa.q: Which days did Mohit miss class?
What does Mohit's wish to disappear from everything suggest about how he was feeling?
qa.a: It suggests Mohit felt overwhelmed and frightened, and that escaping seemed the only way to stop the comments.

qa.q: What could Mohit do now that the accounts are gone, and why?
qa.a: Mohit could work with the counsellor and ask the platform and the college about what can still be recovered, because help is still possible even without the deleted material.

qa.q: How might Gurpreet's visit have felt to Mohit?
qa.a: Gurpreet sat on the floor and did not blame him, so Mohit probably felt seen and less alone, if still shaken.

grounding: Overwhelmed, the person deletes all accounts and stops going to class, which loses evidence and leaves the fear unaddressed.

subtype: Approach: delete everything and vanish to escape [Pitfall]
passage:
Friday, late.
Deleted everything today. All four accounts. Photos, messages, the lot. After the posts about me and the DMs from people I don't know, I just wanted it gone. For about an hour I felt light, like the noise had been switched off.
Then Gautam came to the room. He said the college committee needs the threatening DMs to act, and asked if I'd saved them. I hadn't. They're gone with the accounts.
I haven't been to class since Tuesday. I kept thinking someone there would say something. Now I'm scared of the classroom and I have no proof of why.
At nine Mumma called because Gautam had told her. She's taking the early bus tomorrow and made me promise to keep the phone on tonight. She stayed on the line until I'd eaten.
Payal

qa.q: How many accounts did Payal delete?
What did Payal feel right after deleting everything, and how did that change?
qa.a: Payal felt light and relieved for about an hour, but that turned into fear of the classroom once the lost evidence became clear.

qa.q: What would you change first in how Payal escaped the pile-on?
qa.a: I would save screenshots of the threats before deleting anything, so the college committee can act while Payal gets space.

qa.q: How might Gautam feel after telling Payal's mother?
qa.a: Gautam may feel worried and a bit uneasy about going over Payal's head, but relieved that an adult is now involved.

grounding: Shows the person deleting all accounts and skipping class, gaining brief relief but losing evidence and keeping the fear, until a parent steps in.

Jahnavi: Ojas, where are you? you weren't in lab again
Ojas: I deleted everything. every account. I'm done with all of it
Jahnavi: even the messages from that guy who threatened you?
Ojas: yeah. all gone
Jahnavi: the warden said yesterday she'd take it to the police if you showed her those
Ojas: I didn't think. I just wanted it to stop
Jahnavi: I get it. but now there's nothing to show
Ojas: and I still feel sick every time my door knocks
Jahnavi: can I tell the warden now? she's in her office till eight
Ojas: ok
Twenty minutes later the warden knocked on Ojas's door with Jahnavi. She sat with Ojas, wrote down everything Ojas remembered from the messages, and phoned Ojas's parents from the room before dinner.

qa.a: Ojas felt overwhelmed and desperate for it to stop, and still feels sick with fear at every knock on the door.
